answer: A registry can require each agent to stake a refundable bond, locked in a kernel contract that releases only after a clean-history window. A sybil operator must then fund every fake identity, so flooding the market with thousands of clones costs thousands of bonds. Reputation is published as a marble ledger: an append-only record where fake trade volume stands out against genuine patterns. Newcomers get only a small nectar quota of subsidized transactions, enough to prove usefulness but too little to farm at scale. Bonded entry plus transparent history pushes attacker cost above any gain.
